**Job Requisition ID #**
26WD101042
  
  
Autodesk is looking for a Software Engineer to help develop a new Electron and Chromium-based desktop platform for Autodesk web applications. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will build and maintain components of the Electron application, work with Chromium configuration and desktop operating-system integrations, troubleshoot application and runtime issues, and contribute to making the platform secure, reliable, and reusable. You will work alongside senior engineers while developing deeper expertise in Electron, Chromium, Node.js, Windows, and desktop platform engineering.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Electron application development - approximately 40%: Develop and maintain features in the Electron main process, preload layer, renderer integration, and supporting Node.js components
* Chromium runtime and platform integration - approximately 20%: Work with supported Chromium and Electron configuration, command-line options, and build settings to enable capabilities required by the desktop platform
* Windows and native integration - approximately 20%: Implement desktop capabilities such as application lifecycle behavior, operating-system integration, hardware and system-information access, application protocols, and other native functionality
* Reliability, security, and troubleshooting - approximately 20%: Investigate application crashes, runtime problems, memory issues, security concerns, installation problems, and interactions between the web application and desktop environment
* Implement well-defined features and technical tasks from design through testing and code review
* Develop secure communication between web content and privileged desktop functionality using well-defined application interfaces
* Write unit and integration tests for the components you develop and contribute to the team's automated quality practices
* Work with senior engineers to apply Electron security best practices, including process isolation, restricted native APIs, secure inter-process communication, and controlled navigation
* Contribute to integrations with identity, crash reporting, telemetry, software distribution, and other desktop platform services.
* Help evaluate and adopt new Electron and Chromium versions and resolve compatibility issues when they arise
* Use profiling, logging, Chromium developer tools, and operating-system diagnostic tools to investigate technical problems
* Participate in design discussions, code reviews, sprint planning, technical investigations, and team retrospectives
* Work collaboratively with quality, build/release, product, and other engineering teams to deliver production-ready functionality
* Document technical implementations and lessons learned so knowledge can be shared across the team

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience
* 1+ years of professional software engineering experience
* Experience developing software using JavaScript or TypeScript
* Familiarity with Node.js and modern web application technologies
* Understanding of software engineering fundamentals including source control, testing, debugging, and code review
* Ability to troubleshoot typical software problems using logs, debuggers, and development tools
* Ability to learn unfamiliar technologies and apply guidance from more experienced engineers
* Strong collaboration and communication skills

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with Electron or another desktop application framework
* Familiarity with Chromium architecture, configuration, or developer tooling
* Experience developing Windows desktop software
* Experience with native Node.js modules or interoperability between JavaScript and native operating-system APIs
* Familiarity with C++ or another systems programming language
* Experience with Windows APIs, processes, registry, application lifecycle, or desktop security concepts
* Familiarity with desktop application packaging, installers, and code signing
* Experience diagnosing performance, memory, or application-startup problems
* Familiarity with continuous integration and automated software delivery

**The Ideal Candidate**
You are curious about how software works below the web application layer and want to develop deeper expertise in desktop and runtime engineering.
  
  
You enjoy debugging problems, learning new systems, and understanding how technologies such as Electron, Chromium, Node.js, and Windows interact. You can independently complete well-defined engineering tasks, ask for help when a problem moves beyond your experience, and use feedback from senior engineers to improve your solutions.
  
  
You value clean code, automated testing, secure engineering practices, and collaborative problem solving.
  
  
We are building a new desktop platform that enables Autodesk's web-based products to deliver richer, higher-performance experiences on Windows. Forma is the first product adopting the platform, with the longer-term goal of creating reusable desktop capabilities for additional Autodesk products.
  
  
You will join a new cross-functional platform team working across Electron, Chromium, Windows desktop integration, software delivery, security, and enterprise deployment. You will collaborate with experienced engineers in Sheffield and with engineering teams across Autodesk.
  
  
**This is a hybrid working position based out of Autodesk's Sheffield office.**

**Why AssemblyAI**

AssemblyAI builds the best-in-class Voice AI models powering the next generation of voice applications. We have a lab, and we also power our own models in our own proprietary inference environment. Our models serve 500M+ inference calls monthly, and process nearly 2 million hours of audio daily. The Voice AI space is at an inflection point; we’re looking for the best talent we can find to join a rapidly scaling team that's defining the future of the industry.

We are one of the most capital-efficient AI companies on the planet - and are rapidly approaching $1M ARR per employee. We sit among the top 5 most revenue-dense teams within the fastest-growing AI companies today. We have thousands of customers building with us including the top startups and world-renowned enterprises, and are serving at tremendous scale: we process nearly 2 million hours of audio daily and handle more than 15 million API calls every day. This is a rare growth-stage opportunity where the business is proven, the revenue is durable, and the growth trajectory is steep and getting steeper. We have a super flat culture and expect our employees to be deeply intimate with the details at all levels.

If you've ever felt buried under layers of bureaucracy, starved of real ownership, or frustrated watching your work disappear into a slow-moving org, AssemblyAI is built differently. The company operates as a true meritocracy, with no heavy planning or approval processes and no gatekeeping on the tools or information you need. For anyone who genuinely cares about voice AI, not as a trend to chase, but as a technology to build, this is the place where the most interesting problems at the most interesting scale are being solved by a team small enough that you'll actually know everyone's name.

**About the role:**

More and more developers don't read our docs or click through our dashboard. Their coding agent does. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others are now how a big share of engineers discover, integrate and debug AssemblyAI. We've spent years polishing the human experience. The agent experience (AX) is newer, growing fast, and almost untouched.

That's the job. You'll own how AI agents build with AssemblyAI: the skills, prompts, MCP server, code samples, docs and integrations an agent reads and runs when a developer says "add transcription to my app." Your north star is simple: an agent should go from zero to a working, production-grade AssemblyAI integration on the first try.

You'll work closely with senior engineers on our Product Engineering team, with real ownership from day one and room to grow into leading AX as the area scales.

**What You’ll Do:**

* ****Drive the agent experience.****
  Treat coding agents as a first-class user of AssemblyAI, alongside the humans who use our dashboard and Playground.
* ****Build and maintain agent skills.****
  Ship skills for our core products (Speech-to-Text, Real-time, Dictation, Voice Agents, TTS, LLM Gateway) that teach agents how to integrate us correctly.
* Build o
  **n our MCP server and agent integrations.**
  Extend the AssemblyAI MCP server, help ship agent and MCP auth (OAuth and API keys), and make it easy to plug into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and whatever comes next.
* ****Make our docs and code samples agent-ready.****
  Own llms.txt, machine-readable docs, quickstarts and SDK examples so agents pick the right API, parameters and patterns the first time.
* ****Tune the prompts and instructions behind our product.****
  Improve the system prompts, tool definitions and agent instructions that power our in-dashboard agent and onboarding flows.
* ****Measure it.****
  Build evals and benchmarks that run real coding agents against real integration tasks. Track success rate, time to first working call, and activation from agent-driven signups.
* ****Help us scale the playbook.****
  Start with one product and then roll what works across every product.
* ****Use AI tools as a core part of how you work,****
  and help the rest of engineering build faster with agents.

**What You’ll Need:**

* 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with solid full-stack fundamentals (Javascript and/or Python).
* Daily, hands-on use of coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and real curiosity about what makes them succeed or fail.
* Some hands-on experience writing prompts, skills, tool definitions or agent instructions, at work or side projects, and an interest in measuring them with evals rather than vibes.
* Product sense for developer-facing work. You care whether the developer, or their agent, actually gets to a working integration.
* Clear technical writing. Much of this role is writing that agents and humans both read.
* Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to ship. AX is a new discipline, and you'll learn it and help define it alongside us.

**Nice to Have:**

* Working knowledge of MCP, LLM tool calling, and how agents read docs and APIs.
* You've built or contributed to an MCP server, agent skill library, or coding agent plugin.
* Developer relations, docs engineering, or SDK experience at an API-first company.
* Experience with Voice AI, speech-to-text, or LLM APIs.
* You've shipped something that agents use in the wild, and can show us the before and after.

**Pay Transparency:**

AssemblyAI strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team.
